svg.text: The one verified fault in this swing.

text.tspan: Dashed line: where your hips were at address.
Solid line: your hips at impact, 7% of your body
height closer to the ball.

svg.text: Hip movement toward the ball, address to impact

text.tspan: “It may feel like you stay down, but at
impact your hips have moved toward the ball.”
Your hips moved toward the ball on the way down. At address there was a
clear gap behind you; by impact your hips had moved 7% of your body
height into it, and anything over 4% counts as early extension. When the
hips move forward, your chest rises with them, there is less room for
your arms, and the club tends to arrive thin or pushed right. The most
likely reason is that your lead hip isn’t turning enough: at impact it
had turned 31°, where about 45° is typical. A hip that can’t turn moves
forward instead. Use the wall drill to feel the difference, and the
90/90 hip rotation to give the hip more room to turn.

svg.text: One drill for the fault, one mobility exercise for the cause.
Trail glute stays on the wall

text.tspan: Set up with your backside touching a
wall, or your golf bag. Make slow half
swings and keep your trail glute on the
wall through impact.

svg.text: Fixes: hips moving toward the ball

text.tspan: Sit with both knees bent to 90°, one in
front, one to the side. Rotate slowly to
switch sides, chest tall.
Generic guidance, not medical advice — see a
physiotherapist if you feel pain.
Posture angle changed 6°. It is possible from 5°
and a fault from 9°. A possible fault gets no
drill: film again next session to see if it
holds.
Measured from your hand path, so confidence is capped at medium.
Stored on the AIcoach server until you
delete it. If you don’t save, the clip is
deleted.

g.text: Answers are based only on this analysis.

text.tspan: Why does it feel like I’m staying
down when I’m not?
Your upper body barely changed: your
posture angle moved only 6°, so it
feels like you stay down. What moved
is lower. In your impact frame your
hips are 7% of your body height
closer to the ball than at address.
You can’t feel that from inside the
swing, which is why the wall drill
helps: if your backside leaves the
wall, you’ll know.
Should I change my grip as
well?
I can’t tell you that. This analysis
didn’t measure your grip, so I won’t
guess. A coach can check it in
person.

g.text: How do I know the drill is working?
Can I do this drill in a net?

text.tspan: The pro stays beside your lesson card as you
scroll. It only uses this analysis: no new
